title: THE FIRST FRAME
goal: Catch the thought before it becomes the room.

steps.action: A trigger flickers.
Do not explain it yet.
Pin the first thought, picture, or prediction exactly as it arrived.
Put quotation marks around it.
The catch ends there; no life story, no courtroom, no spiral.

win: ✓ One thought stayed one thought; the courtroom never opened.
supports: Exhale after “Close Capture”; loosen the label.
I can use “Pause Story” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Trigger → Pause Story → Capture Thought → Quote → Close Capture
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if holding the thought in mind makes you feel less steady or more upset.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.

steps.action: Imagine two trays.
Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.

win: ✓ Both trays stayed visible; the verdict stopped being one-sided.
supports: Exhale after “Balance Verdict”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Name Sides” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Imagine Trays → Name Sides → Sort Facts → Switch Sides → Balance Verdict
safety:
PAUSE
Quit when you are recycling arguments instead of discovering evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.

steps.action: Picture the feared ending in one line.
Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
Move through the five steps once in your mind.
Then take the first coping action available now.

win: ✓ The forecast lost its monopoly.
supports: Exhale after “Act Now”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Build Exits” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Name Fear → Build Exits → Add Likely → Climb Route → Act Now
safety:
PAUSE
Do not run this alone for immediate danger, medical crisis, or trauma flooding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE GREY DIAL
goal: Binary thinking hates a numbered dial.

steps.action: Name the two extremes your mind is using.
Build a 0–10 scale between them and say three real anchor points: 2, 5, and 8.
Place today’s event where the evidence fits—not where the emotion shouts.
Choose a response matched to that exact setting.

win: ✓ The dial found a middle, and the response found its size.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Response”; keep both sides.
I can use “Build Scale” before concluding.
formula_flow: Name Extremes → Build Scale → Place Today → Choose Response
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if grading becomes another perfection test.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THEIR MIRROR
goal: Use the standard you reserve for someone you respect.

steps.action: Imagine a trusted person bringing you the same facts.
Hold the questions you would ask them, the allowances you would make, and the evidence you would require before judging them.
Now remove their name.
Apply that page to yourself without adding a harsher clause.

win: ✓ The label lost some of its legal power.
supports: Exhale after “Apply Page”; loosen the label.
I can use “Offer Allowances” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Imagine Trusted → Offer Allowances → Remove Name → Apply Page
safety:
PAUSE
Leave the mirror if it excuses harm or becomes forced positivity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE RULE UNDER THE RULE
goal: A surface thought often works for a hidden constitution.

steps.action: Picture the painful thought.
Ask, ‘If that were true, what would it mean about me, others, or life?’ Answer quickly, then ask the same question of the answer.
Continue only until one stable rule repeats.
Put that rule in a mental box.
Today’s task is to inspect it, not obey it.

win: ✓ I inspected the hidden rule without obeying it.
supports: Exhale after “Apply Today”; release the score.
I can use “Ask Meaning” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Picture Painful → Ask Meaning → Continue Stable → Box Rule → Apply Today
safety:
PAUSE
Stop descent if it triggers feeling unreal or disconnected, hopelessness, or overwhelming material.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SCHEMA CONTRABAND FILE
goal: Smuggle what does not fit reality past the old filter.

steps.action: Catch one event your negative self-story would normally delete.
Say what happened, why it really does not fit the old rule, and which convenient excuse the rule will use to dismiss it.
Sign the entry as usable evidence and reread it tomorrow once—no chanting.

win: ✓ The story became one version instead of the constitution.
supports: I can use “Describe Happened” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Capture → Describe Happened → Sign
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use exceptions to deny real problems that need action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FORECAST SCOREBOARD
goal: Memory edits its predictions after the result.

steps.action: Before an uncertain event, remember four items: prediction, confidence %, deadline, and what counts as a hit.
Afterward, hold the result without rewriting the original entry.
Calculate the gap between confidence and reality.
After five rounds, look for your recurring bias.

win: ✓ Forecast bias exposed. Memory cannot quietly rewrite the scoreboard now.
supports: Exhale after “Spot the Bias”; release the score.
What lost power: “Count Hit” → “Spot the Bias”?
I can use “Keep Result” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Count Hit → Keep Result → Calculate → Spot the Bias
safety:
PAUSE
Retire the ledger if it feeds compulsive monitoring.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SKY DOES NOT BECOME THE WEATHER
goal: Content changes; the capacity to notice keeps showing up.

steps.action: Name one thought, one feeling, and one role active now.
For each, say: ‘This is being noticed.’ Search for the noticing itself—its colour, age, or mood.
If none can be found, rest with that openness for ten seconds.
Return by feeling both feet.

win: ✓ Weather moved; the sky stayed. Both feet found the room again.
supports: Exhale after “Land in Feet”; keep the compass.
I can use “Say Being” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Name Thought → Say Being → Rest Openness → Land in Feet
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid prolonged self-inquiry if it intensifies feeling unreal or detached from yourself or unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TRANSLATE THE VERDICT
goal: ‘Bad’ is compressed data. Decompress it.

steps.action: Take one judgement and mentally translate it into three components: visible facts, personal preference, likely consequence.
Example: ‘Awful meeting’ becomes ‘Two interruptions; I prefer turn-taking; the decision stayed unclear.’ Respond to the components rather than fighting the label.

win: ✓ I unpacked the verdict into facts I could actually respond to.
supports: Exhale after “Prefer Decision”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Prefer Decision” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Take Judgement → Prefer Decision
safety:
PAUSE
Keep moral language where clear ethical wrongdoing must be named.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE CRISIS MENU
goal: Choose before distress turns choice into fog.

steps.action: Prepare five ten-minute diversions across different channels: hands, movement, sound, practical task, safe contact.
During a spike, select the first available option without browsing for the perfect one.
Finish the interval, reassess safety, then either return or choose support.

win: ✓ Distress no longer has to invent the menu while it is hungry.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Interval”; release the score.
I can use “Select Option” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Prepare Five → Select Option → Finish Interval
safety:
PAUSE
Diversion is not enough for suicidal intent, violence risk, overdose, or medical emergency.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: UPGRADE THE WAITING ROOM
goal: An unavoidable minute can still change quality.

steps.action: Pick one lever for this interval: picture a supportive scene, connect the moment to meaning, offer a brief prayer, relax one area, or do one thing fully.
Use only one lever until the interval ends.
You are improving the room, not denying why you are there.

win: ✓ I upgraded the waiting minute without pretending I wanted to be there.
supports: Gently exhale after “Upgrade the Minute”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Use Lever” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Pick Best → Use Lever → Upgrade the Minute
safety:
PAUSE
Move from coping to problem-solving when the situation requires direct action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DOES THE FEELING FIT THE FILE?
goal: Emotion deserves respect; facts determine the dose.

steps.action: Separate four cards: prompting event, meaning, verified evidence, actual present threat.
Compare the emotion’s intensity and duration with the fourth card.
If they fit, use the feeling’s message.
If they exceed it, regulate first and update the meaning.

win: ✓ Feeling respected; dosage handed back to the facts.
supports: Exhale after “Update Meaning”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Compare Emotion” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Separate Cards → Compare Emotion → Use Feeling → Update Meaning
safety:
PAUSE
Trust immediate protective action when evidence shows real threat.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REVERSE THE URGE, COMPLETELY
goal: When the emotion is unjustified, half-opposites do not retrain it.

steps.action: Verify that the facts do not support the action impulse.
Then do its full safe opposite: approach instead of avoid, speak gently instead of attack, straighten instead of collapse, engage instead of hide.
Match posture, words, and behaviour until the new signal is coherent.

win: ✓ Desire got a seat, not the steering wheel.
supports: Exhale after “Match Posture”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Speak Gently” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Check Support → Speak Gently → Match Posture
safety:
PAUSE
Never oppose an urge that correctly protects you from danger or violation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: URGE IS NOT EMOTION
goal: Separate the weather from what it pushes you to do.

steps.action: Label the emotion in one word.
Name every behaviour it is urging—text, withdraw, shout, spend, hide, check.
Notice each SAFE, COSTLY, or UNCLEAR.
Select a low-risk move that respects the emotion without automatically enacting its favourite instruction.

win: ✓ The feeling stayed as weather; the urge lost its marching orders.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Safe”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Hide Name” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Name Emotion → Hide Name → Safe → Choose Safe
safety:
PAUSE
Get support if impulses involve harm, intoxication, or loss of control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
goal: Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.

steps.action: Spot the current chapter only: sensation, meaning, action urge, or settling.
Permit the next natural chapter while withholding later ones.
If sensation is active, do not interpret; if meaning is clear, do not act yet.
Continue until a genuine settling marker—breath change, warmth, tears ending, posture release—appears.

win: ✓ One emotional chapter reached a real ending marker.
supports: Exhale after “Continue Genuine”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Permit” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Identify Chapter → Permit → Pause Meaning → Continue Genuine
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the process floods awareness or removes action control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: INSTALL THE CAPABLE MEMORY
goal: A resource becomes usable once it receives a body address.

steps.action: Recall one real moment of courage, care, steadiness, or help.
Find its strongest sensory detail and the body location that responds.
Add a small gesture while the memory is vivid.
Release, then use the gesture once to see whether the quality returns.

win: ✓ The capable state became easier to call back on purpose.
supports: Gently exhale after “Release Gesture”; orient to now.
I can use “Find Strongest” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Recall Real → Find Strongest → Add Small → Release Gesture
safety:
PAUSE
Choose a different memory if the scene contains mixed threat or grief.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAMP WHERE THE DETAIL CAME FROM
goal: A memory matters without every detail carrying equal certainty.

steps.action: Choose one small memory detail; do not replay the event.
Stamp it SENSED, INFERRED, LEARNED LATER, or UNSURE.
Give the detail a confidence word—high, medium, low, or unknown—based on its source rather than its emotional intensity.
Picture one core fact that remains reliable and let the other detail keep its honest uncertainty.

win: ✓ The memory kept a reliable core and honest fog around the rest.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Core”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Tag Source” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Pick Detail → Tag Source → Rate Confidence → Keep Core
safety:
PAUSE
Do not force missing details; stop and seek support if the memory becomes overwhelming or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OCEAN IN THE THROAT
goal: Use barely audible sound as a pace rail.

steps.action: Narrow the throat only enough to create a soft ocean texture, never a rasp.
Let that sound accompany an easy inhale and exhale.
Reduce effort until someone beside you might barely hear it.
After several waves, release the technique completely.

win: ✓ Technique released. The calmer pace can stand on its own.
supports: Exhale after “Release Technique”; then keep moving.
I can use “Let Sound” before motivation.
formula_flow: Create Soft → Let Sound → Reduce Effort → Release Technique
safety:
PAUSE
Do not practise through irritation, constriction, breathing illness, or dizziness.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: INSTALL THE COUNTER-QUALITY
goal: Do not wrestle a harmful tendency on its own ground.

steps.action: Name the active pattern and the wholesome quality opposite with it: cruelty/kindness, panic/steadiness, greed/sufficiency.
Produce one thought, posture, and act expressing the counter-quality.
Keep it credible rather than grand.
Train the opposite channel through embodiment.

win: ✓ The opposite quality got a real body, not just a good intention.
supports: I can use “Act Counter” before motivation.
formula_flow: Name Active → Act Counter → Keep Credible → Train
safety:
PAUSE
Countering must not suppress valid grief, anger, or protective fear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ERASE THE OBJECT, KEEP THE CONTACT
goal: Let focus outlive its original target.

steps.action: Stabilise attention on one simple form.
Gradually remove its name, meaning, shape, and boundary in that order.
Preserve the ongoing sense of attending as the object loses definition.
Rest briefly with contact that no longer depends on a clear thing.

win: ✓ The load became a sequence instead of a wall.
supports: Exhale after “Rest Briefly”; release extra load.
I can use “Remove Name” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Stabilise → Remove Name → Attend Object → Rest Briefly
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid object dissolution when prone to derealisation or perceptual instability.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE FIRST ‘I’
goal: Sense of ‘I’ has an entrance point.

steps.action: Notice an experience before describing it.
Wait for the moment ‘I,’ ‘mine,’ or ‘about me’ attaches.
Trace that addition to a body sensation, image, or location.
Observe the attachment without removing it.
The task is detection, not metaphysical victory.

win: ✓ I found the ‘I’ without needing to solve who ‘I’ ultimately am.
supports: Gently exhale after “Do the Task”; no forcing.
I can use “Wait Moment” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Experience → Wait Moment → Trace Addition → Observe Attachment → Do the Task
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the search produces feeling unreal or detached from yourself or panic.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FIVE-LAYER INSPECTION
goal: Identity may be wearing several visible coats.

steps.action: Move through body, energy, mind, intellect, and deep ease.
At each layer ask what is present, what changes, and how it is known.
Do not discard any layer.
Place them like translucent sheets within awareness, then select the layer needed for practical action.

win: ✓ Five layers became one usable next layer.
supports: Gently exhale after “Place Like”; no forcing.
“Keep All Layers” keeps sensation as data.
I can use “Ask Change” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Move Body → Ask Change → Keep All Layers → Place Like
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid abstract layer work when immediate grounding is needed.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
goal: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.

steps.action: Take one rigid reading of an event.
Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed.
Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes.

win: ✓ Another person’s response moved out of the judge’s chair.
supports: Exhale after “Try Construction”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Compare Dream” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Take Event → Compare Dream → Identify Facts → Try Construction
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid dreamlike framing if it increases derealisation or psychotic symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN THE PROJECTION TO SENDER
goal: The mind may be viewing its expectation on someone else’s screen.

steps.action: Picture the quality you are assigning outward.
Ask what internal expectation, fear, or rule would make that quality especially visible.
Name the external evidence separately.
Keep what the facts support; return the excess meaning to your own inquiry.

win: ✓ Facts stayed; the extra projection went back for review.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Facts”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Ask Internal” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Quality → Ask Internal → Name External → Keep Facts
safety:
PAUSE
Projection analysis must not erase another person’s documented behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE ONE LENS, WATCH THE WORLD
goal: Experience partly inherits the meaning that organises it.

steps.action: Choose a current event and picture the lens being used.
Replace it with one plausible alternative—not a positive slogan.
Spend five minutes acting from the alternate lens and observe changes in body, attention, and available choices.

win: ✓ I changed one lens and watched the available choices change with it.
supports: Gently exhale after “Act Lens”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Replace Plausible” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Choose Event → Replace Plausible → Act Lens
safety:
PAUSE
Retain the original lens when evidence confirms danger or wrongdoing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BOX THE PROBLEM
goal: Scattered distress cannot be solved because it has no edges.

steps.action: Picture three lines: CURRENT CONDITION; DESIRED CONDITION; MEASURABLE GAP.
Remove history unless it changes the gap.
Give the problem a time horizon and one owner.
If the statement still contains ‘everything,’ shrink it again.

win: ✓ I boxed the problem until ‘everything’ could no longer fit inside it.
supports: I can use “Remove History” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Picture Lines → Remove History → Give Problem → Statement
safety:
PAUSE
Some pain needs witnessing rather than conversion into a problem.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIXED, FLEXIBLE, UNKNOWN, ASSUMED
goal: Obstacles demand different tools depending on their category.

steps.action: Name every barrier.
Mark each barrier as fixed, flexible, unknown, or assumed.
Accept the fixed, negotiate the flexible, investigate the unknown, and test the assumed.
Begin with the highest-impact item whose category permits movement.

win: ✓ Care stayed; over-ownership did not.
supports: Exhale after “Start What Moves”; release extra load.
I can use “Mark Category” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Name → Mark Category → Test Assumed → Start What Moves
safety:
PAUSE
Reclassify when new evidence changes a limit’s status.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM
goal: Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.

steps.action: Start a brief timer and generate options without ranking, explaining, or defending them.
Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one strange-but-safe possibility.
Only after the timer ends may feasibility enter the room.

win: ✓ I let options multiply before judgement was allowed into the room.
supports: Exhale after “Test Feasibility”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Include Conventional” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Start Brief → Include Conventional → Test Feasibility
safety:
PAUSE
Exclude choices that violate ethics, consent, law, or safety from the start.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DECIDE THE STOPPING LINE FIRST
goal: Analysis cannot finish if ‘enough’ has no definition.

steps.action: Before researching, state the minimum evidence required to choose: number of quotes, critical facts, confidence level, or deadline.
Picture what would really reverse the decision.
When the threshold is met, select; further information needs a new reason for entry.

win: ✓ Clarity survived the emotion.
supports: Exhale after “Select Further”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Picture Genuinely” without extra heat.
formula_flow: State Minimum → Picture Genuinely → Select Further
safety:
PAUSE
Raise the threshold for hard to undo or high-stakes decisions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
goal: Residual body alarm is not fresh evidence.

steps.action: Set a reasonable after-event window during which shakiness, replay, fatigue, or emotion are expected echoes.
Picture its end time.
Until then, keep sensations but forbid them from changing your meaning of what happened.
Reassess after recovery and sleep where possible.

win: ✓ I recognised the aftershock as residue, not fresh evidence.
supports: I can use “Picture Time” before motivation.
formula_flow: Set Reasonable → Picture Time → Notice Sensations → Reassess
safety:
PAUSE
Seek care when symptoms are severe, worsening, or medically concerning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
goal: Analysis may keep interrupting an unfinished inner sequence.

steps.action: Bring up the image gently and prohibit verbal commentary.
Allow it to move at its own speed until it reaches a stable frame or natural ending.
Notice whether your position, distance, or available action changes.
Reorient afterward using present sensory facts.

win: ✓ I let the image reach its last frame instead of interrupting it with analysis.
supports: Exhale after “Use Sensory”; notice the room.
“Check Your Position” proves the present returned.
I can use “Allow Move” to return here.
formula_flow: Bring Image → Allow Move → Check Your Position → Use Sensory
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use alone with traumatic imagery, hallucinations, or destabilisation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.

steps.action: The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
State the size and direction of the error.
Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.

win: ✓ Original prediction preserved. Hindsight cannot edit the miss now.
supports: Exhale after “Preserve Forecast”; slow the clock.
“Keep Both Versions” to “Preserve Forecast”: what loosened?
I can use “State Size” without rushing.
formula_flow: Keep Both Versions → State Size → Name Miss → Preserve Forecast
safety:
PAUSE
Do not overlearn from one noisy or unrepresentative result.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
goal: Certainty and support need separate meters.

steps.action: Rate how sure you feel from 0–100.
Independently rate evidence quality using source reliability, directness, and recency.
Picture the two scores on separate meters so certainty cannot masquerade as evidence.
Let the evidence meter choose the action; treat the confidence meter as a feeling to notice, not a vote.

win: ✓ Evidence got the vote. Confidence stayed a feeling.
supports: Exhale after “Follow Evidence”; end the lap.
I can use “Rate Evidence” without another lap.
formula_flow: Rate Sure → Rate Evidence → Separate Meters → Follow Evidence
safety:
PAUSE
Urgent protective instincts may require action while evidence is gathered.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT AN EXPIRY DATE ON THE CONCLUSION
goal: Old evidence should not command new conditions forever.

steps.action: Estimate how quickly the conclusion’s evidence can become stale.
Give it a renewal date plus the data required then.
Until review, use it temporaryly; after expiry, it must be renewed by current evidence before influencing behaviour.

win: ✓ The story now has to coexist with what does not fit.
supports: Exhale after “Use Temporaryly”; end the lap.
I can use “Give Renewal” without another lap.
formula_flow: Estimate Quickly → Give Renewal → Use Temporaryly
safety:
PAUSE
Stable facts do not need artificial expiry simply to reduce discomfort.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS
goal: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.

steps.action: Keep all observations fixed.
Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
For each, spot the one simple action it recommends.
Compare which action remains robust across versions.

win: ✓ Three premises produced three worlds; only the robust action survived all of them.
supports: Exhale after “Compare Action”; keep both sides.
I can use “Reframe Three Ways” before concluding.
formula_flow: Keep Observations → Reframe Three Ways → Identify Action → Compare Action
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid invented alternatives that contradict established evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FORECAST WITH A LANDING ZONE
goal: Accuracy can include an honest margin of error.

steps.action: Predict a range rather than a perfect point.
State the acceptable error band and why it is reasonable.
After the result, measure reality check: inside, near, or outside the band.
Adjust future range width instead of declaring success or failure.

win: ✓ The forecast became a range, so reality had somewhere honest to land.
supports: Exhale after “Widen the Landing”; release the score.
“Widen the Landing”: what changed from “Predict Range”?
I can use “State Acceptable” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Predict Range → State Acceptable → Measure Reality → Widen the Landing
safety:
PAUSE
Keep tight limits where safety or engineering precision requires them.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WAIT FOR THE EVIDENCE THAT CAN EXIST
goal: Some decisions are early because their key fact has not been born.

steps.action: Name the future information that could really change the choice, when it becomes available, and how each possible result would alter action.
Wait only for that evidence.
Everything else is delay wearing a research badge.

win: ✓ I stopped researching a fact that does not exist yet.
supports: Exhale after “Reject Delay”; end the lap.
I can use “Wait Evidence” without another lap.
formula_flow: Name Future → Wait Evidence → Reject Delay
safety:
PAUSE
Act with current information if delay itself creates material risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY
goal: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.

steps.action: Hold the trigger at a manageable centre.
Without looking away, name five simultaneous peripheral details—colour, distance, movement, light, geometry.
Let central and surrounding information coexist until the scene feels larger than the alarm.

win: ✓ The threat stayed visible without swallowing the whole scene.
supports: One exhale after “Let Central”; redirect attention.
I can use “Look Away” amid noise.
formula_flow: Hold Trigger → Look Away → Let Central
safety:
PAUSE
Do not keep a dangerous cue in view when withdrawal is the safer action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE NOVELTY TO THE RIGHT TEAM
goal: Do not fight stimulation seeking; recruit it.

steps.action: Spot the novelty source pulling attention away.
Add controlled variety to the desired task instead: change order, tool, location, soundtrack, colour, or challenge.
Keep the goal constant while refreshing the route.

win: ✓ Novelty joined the mission instead of stealing it.
supports: One exhale after “Keep Goal”; redirect attention.
I can use “Add Controlled” amid noise.
formula_flow: Identify Novelty → Add Controlled → Keep Goal
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid novelty additions that reduce accuracy or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PIN A RETURN ADDRESS
goal: A distraction should cost one return address, not a full reconstruction.

steps.action: Name the exact OBJECT currently carrying the task: document, pan, form, email, shelf, or tool.
Notice the precise LOCATION inside it: paragraph three, top-left field, second burner, or blue tab.
Choose one NEXT VERB for that location: compare, type, turn, check, send, or place.
After the interruption, say the three-part address once and act on the verb without rescanning the entire task.

win: ✓ Autopilot missed its usual handoff.
formula_flow: Name Object → Place → Choose Verb → Reenter
safety:
PAUSE
Do not rely on a return address for driving, medication, machinery, clinical procedures, or tasks requiring a complete safety recheck.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
goal: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.

steps.action: Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty. Put it into simple words a child could understand.
Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.

win: ✓ No feeling agreed, but no red line had to be betrayed.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Survivor”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Vetoes” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Seat Feelings → Vetoes → Clear Board → Choose Survivor
safety:
PAUSE
Safety, consent, law, and basic care outrank every emotional veto; seek support if no safe move remains.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ADD THE TEMPORARY CLAUSE
goal: A temporary state does not get to write your permanent biography.

steps.action: Append this qualifier to the self-judgement: ‘in this state, under these conditions, for now.’ Name the state and conditions precisely.
Then spot one condition likely to change and one action that could influence it.

win: ✓ I added ‘for now’ and reopened the future.
supports: Exhale after “Identify Condition”; end the lap.
I can use “Identify Condition” without another lap.
formula_flow: State Conditions → Identify Condition
safety:
PAUSE
Seek assessment when a serious or persistent condition needs care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PRACTISE THE QUALITY ANONYMOUSLY
goal: You can enact a disowned strength before claiming it.

steps.action: Choose a positive quality that feels ‘not me.’ do one behaviour expressing it without telling anyone or using the quality word.
Ask the brave question, make the playful Notice, accept the compliment, offer the clear boundary.
Let evidence arrive before identity approval.

win: ✓ Identity stopped gatekeeping a quality that already worked.
supports: Exhale after “Let Proof Arrive”; release extra load.
I can use “Ask Brave” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Choose Positive → Ask Brave → Let Proof Arrive
safety:
PAUSE
Select a safe, values-consistent expression rather than a performative stunt.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: POWER THEN, RESOURCES NOW
goal: Past helplessness should not inherit present equipment.

steps.action: Imagine two sides.
On the first side, picture your age, knowledge, money, power, support, and choices then.
On the second side, picture the same things today.
Notice what gives you more choice now.
Pick one resource you have today and use it in one small action.

win: ✓ The past kept its history; today’s resources entered the scene.
supports: Exhale after “Use One Resource”; end the lap.
“Find The Change” proves loops can stop.
I can use “Then” without another lap.
formula_flow: Imagine Two Sides → Then → Picture Today → Find The Change → Use One Resource
safety:
PAUSE
Acknowledge areas where present power is still limited.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE PROGRESS LEAVE FOOTPRINTS
goal: Effort is hard to trust when completion disappears.

steps.action: Choose a marker for each finished unit: move a bead, fill a square, stack a card, close a ticket, place a clip.
The marker must represent real completion, not time spent.
Let the growing trail provide feedback.

win: ✓ Progress left tracks. Effort is visible now.
supports: Exhale after “See the Trail”; release extra blame.
I can use “Marker” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Choose Marker → Marker → See the Trail
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid turning markers into compulsive counting or vanity metrics.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
goal: The body can stop rehearsing defeat before facts arrive.

steps.action: Take a stable, non-defensive position: feet supported, spine available, gaze level, arms unguarded enough for safety.
Do not use the posture to predict success or failure.
Keep the posture while you wait for actual evidence.

win: ✓ Posture held steady while prophecy waited outside.
supports: Exhale after “Hold for Evidence”; then keep moving.
I can use “Refuse Prophecy” before motivation.
formula_flow: Adopt → Hold the Posture
safety:
PAUSE
Choose protective posture and distance in genuinely threatening settings.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE SHAKE BE SMALL
goal: Trembling is movement, not automatic evidence of collapse.

steps.action: If medically safe and oriented, permit a small tremor rather than clamping it down.
Track its location, rhythm, and whether choice remains intact.
Let it stop, continue, or migrate without exaggeration.
Ground when the movement ends.

win: ✓ The shake stayed small enough to finish being a shake.
supports: Gently exhale after “Let Shake Finish”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Track Location” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Medically → Track Location → Let Migrate → Let Shake Finish
safety:
PAUSE
Seek medical attention for unexplained, severe, persistent, or concerning tremor.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE TEMPERATURE FACTS
goal: Imagined danger must coexist with actual thermal evidence.

steps.action: Check temperature at three locations: hands, face, and where clothing meets skin.
Use comparative language—cooler, warmer, neutral—rather than guessing degrees.
Let the three readings define the body’s current climate.

win: ✓ The body’s current climate replaced the imagined forecast.
supports: Exhale after “Let Readings”; notice the room.
I can use “Use Comparative” to return here.
formula_flow: Check Temperature → Use Comparative → Let Readings
safety:
PAUSE
Seek care for abnormal temperature, numbness, burns, or medical symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SCENT THE RETURN
goal: Train one neutral aroma to accompany successful orientation within the current setting.

steps.action: Take a mild, distinctive scent that feels safe.
Apply it only after you have really returned to present time and choice.
Pair it with date, place, and one grounding action across several occasions.
Later, test whether the scent helps retrieve that state.

win: ✓ I paired one neutral scent with the route back to the present.
supports: Exhale after “Test Whether”; notice the room.
I can use “Use After” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose Safe → Use After → Date Grounding → Test Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid allergens, pregnancy-sensitive scents, substance cues, and public exposure concerns.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE RINGS OF AGENCY
goal: Do not spend control effort in the observation ring.

steps.action: Imagine three rings: CONTROL, INFLUENCE, WATCH.
Put each piece of the problem in the right ring in your mind.
Do one thing you control, make one request where you have influence, and let go of one thing you can only watch.

win: ✓ I acted in one ring, asked in one ring, and stopped fighting the third.
supports: Exhale after “Take Action”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Place Each Part” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Imagine Three Rings → Place Each Part → Take Action
safety:
PAUSE
Observation still requires protective action when risk indicators appear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE VALUE TO A NEW VESSEL
goal: Loss may destroy the channel, not the underlying value.

steps.action: Name what the lost person, role, place, or ability allowed you to express—care, mastery, belonging, beauty, service.
Find a different, honest channel for a small portion of that value.
Begin without treating substitution as replacement.

win: ✓ The value found a new vessel without pretending nothing was lost.
supports: I can use “Find Different” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Name Lost → Find Different → Start
safety:
PAUSE
Do not rush reconstruction before the loss has been acknowledged.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE THE ORDINARY WORTHY OF FULL CONTACT
goal: Sacredness can be an attention quality, not an exceptional event.

steps.action: Choose one routine act—making tea, bathing, preparing a child’s bag, opening work.
do it without rushing or secondary media.
Notice craft, dependence, and life supported by the act.
Finish as if it deserved completion.

win: ✓ Ordinary task, full contact. It got the finish it deserved.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Deserved”; slow the clock.
formula_flow: Choose Routine → Perform → Craft → Finish Deserved
safety:
PAUSE
Keep pace appropriate when practical urgency is real.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CATCH THE MOMENT ‘MINE’ ARRIVES
goal: Ownership may be added after experience begins.

steps.action: Wait for a sensation or thought to appear.
Notice its first instant, then watch for the extra sense of ‘my thought,’ ‘my pain,’ or ‘about me.’ Notice the interval between appearance and possession without trying to change it.

win: ✓ Experience arrived first. Ownership arrived second.
supports: Exhale after “Catch Ownership”; watch the thought.
I can use “Catch Ownership” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Wait Sensation → Catch Ownership
safety:
PAUSE
Use first-person sensory grounding when self-distance feels destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.

steps.action: Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.

win: ✓ The emotional stack revealed which block was actually carrying the weight.
supports: Exhale after “Rebuild Stack”; mark the pause.
I can use “Pull One” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Name Stack → Pull One → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the game causes numbness, feeling unreal or disconnected, suppression, or pressure to erase a valid feeling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
goal: The future should not be rehearsed as a single locked corridor.

steps.action: Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene.
Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
Notice the cost and value of each.
Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values.

win: ✓ The compass still works even when the landscape hurts.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Best”; keep the compass.
I can use “Create Endings” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Identify Critical → Create Endings → Cost → Keep Best
safety:
PAUSE
Do not imagine unsafe endings merely to increase variety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COMMON IS NOT THE SAME AS RIGHT
goal: Frequency cannot settle an ethical question.

steps.action: State the social norm and your chosen criteria—harm, fairness, consent, dignity, responsibility.
Check the norm against each criterion without citing popularity.
Keep, modify, or reject it based on the ethical comparison.

win: ✓ Popularity lost the argument the moment ethics entered the room.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Modify”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “Evaluate” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: State Social → Evaluate → Keep Modify
safety:
PAUSE
Consult affected communities and expertise when personal criteria are incomplete.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS
goal: A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.

steps.action: Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned.
Check whether you still endorse that standard.
Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source.

win: ✓ The repair stayed mine. The inherited shame went home.
supports: Exhale after “Keep Repair”; release extra blame.
I can use “Ask Whether” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Identify Whose → Ask Whether → Keep Repair
safety:
PAUSE
Seek support when shame is severe, trauma-linked, or tied to self-harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
